transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-16
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Huang (Redwood SE), Marcus Reed (CTO - Nova), Priya Shah (Lead ML Eng - Nova), Derek Lang (Infra - Nova)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on latency & throughput targets for Nova Payments' realtime fraud / authorization assistant. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) for p95 SLAs and predictable concurrency. Next steps: pricing, SOC2 & security docs, benchmark run.

Topics:
- p95 latency targets and how they change with sequence length/concurrency
- streaming vs non-streaming token-level throughput (tokens/sec)
- concurrency, batching, and KV/prefix cache implications
- Dedicated capacity guarantees and private deployment (VPC/KMS) checklist

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh i'm Samir from Redwood, i'll kick us off. lena from our se team is here. could you quick intro?
[00:15] Marcus: yeah Marcus Reed, CTO at Nova Payments, thanks. we're looking at real-time decisioning for auth flows, so latency is huge.
[00:25] Priya: Priya here, i run the model infra and ops, we have a 150ms p95 target on simple prompts and ~300ms for richer context, depends on concurrency.
[00:40] Lena: thanks, that helps. can you say a bit about typical prompt length and token distribution?
[00:50] Priya: mostly short, 20-80 tokens. but when we include transaction history + device signals some go up to 250 tokens. typical mix is ~70% <50 tokens, 25% 50-150, 5% >150.
[01:10] Samir: perfect. when you say p95 150ms, is that end-to-end including network?
[01:18] Priya: yes, from our service to model response visible to user. we need to account for deserialization + enrichment.
[01:26] Derek: and we expect concurrency bursts during peak hours, up to 400 concurrent small requests for auth checks, sustained 100-200 normally.
[01:40] Lena: good, so two axes: single-request p95 and sustained concurrency throughput. for hosted we can often meet low-latency if you pick smaller models and streaming, but dedicated gives predictable tail latency at scale.
[02:00] Marcus: can you explain streaming vs non-streaming in your runtime? we care about first-token latency and token/sec for longer prompts.
[02:09] Lena: sure. streaming returns tokens as they're generated — first token arrives faster because we don't wait for full decode. token/sec throughput matters for longer sequences; on our runtime you can expect roughly 1000-1500 tokens/sec per GPU for medium models with quantization and batching offload, but that varies by model and sequence length. first token can be 30-120ms on dedicated infra for small models.
[02:35] Priya: 1000-1500 tokens/sec per GPU sounds good, but how does that translate to p95 for a 50-token prompt at concurrency 200?
[02:45] Lena: rough math: if each GPU gives 1200 tokens/sec, 50 tokens is ~42ms of raw generation. but you also have decode overhead, batching, network, so p95 ends up closer to 150-200ms on a dedicated pool optimized for low-latency with small batch sizes. when concurrency is high we rely on autoscaling or dedicated shard pools to maintain SLO.
[03:10] Marcus: what's the difference between hosted and dedicated in latency guarantees?
[03:17] Samir: hosted is multi-tenant; typical p95s are competitive but not SLA-backed. Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and guaranteed capacity, plus fine-tuned kernel selection and batching configs to meet p95 targets. private (VPC/on-prem) mirrors dedicated but with network & KMS under your control.
[03:38] Derek: for private, how do we manage KV cache and prefix caching? we need cold-start behavior minimized.
[03:45] Lena: we support persistent KV caches per deployment — you can pin shards or use warm pools. cold starts can cost a few hundred ms; warm pools cut that to tens of ms. also our runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache reuse to reduce token cost and e2e latency.
[04:05] Priya: can we run a token/sec benchmark with our prompts? we want to see p95 curves at 50, 100, 200 concurrency and streaming vs non-streaming.
[04:12] Samir: absolutely. lena will share a benchmark harness. typical process is: you give sample prompt mix, we run distributed token/sec & latency tests on hosted and dedicated, and we share logs + plots.
[04:25] Marcus: and for security we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS integration, and data residency. how does private help?
[04:34] Samir: private lets you run the control plane in your VPC or on-prem with customer-managed KMS/HSM, full audit logs, and integration with your SSO. we have SOC2 docs for hosted and dedicated; private adds network isolation for compliance. we'll share the checklist.
[04:50] Lena: from infra perspective, we can also support bring-your-own-key and table-level encryption for logs. our private deployments have connectors to common KMS providers.
[05:02] Derek: what about throughput cost tradeoffs — like batching increases throughput but can increase tail latency. how do you recommend tuning?
[05:11] Lena: yes exactly. small batch sizes (1-8) keep latency low but waste some GPU throughput; larger batches (16-64) increase tokens/sec at cost of p95. we surface recommendations per workload in Redwood Optimize; we can run profiling to suggest batching/quantize settings and kernel selection.
[05:30] Priya: do you support quantized models? our priority is cost but we can't sacrifice accuracy for fraud detection.
[05:37] Samir: we support int8/4 quantization profiles and give quality regression monitoring. for fraud, we usually recommend trying int8 first and running evals; if you see regressions, we can pin float16 or hybrid.
[05:50] Marcus: ok, timeline — if we want a pilot on dedicated, what's realistic?
[05:56] Samir: pilot can start in 2-4 weeks once contracts are in place; provisioning GPUs & a dedicated pool takes ~3-5 business days; private deployments take longer due to networking and KMS — plan 4-8 weeks.
[06:10] Priya: for the benchmark, can you expose per-token timing so we can compute token/sec and p95 by token index?
[06:18] Lena: yes, we can provide per-token latency traces and breakdown: kernel time, KV fetch, compile time, network. sometimes the transcripts have small mislabels but the timing data is raw.
[06:30] Derek: any gotchas on network — p95 measurement needs to account for NAT gateways and our edge routing.
[06:36] Samir: good point, recommend running benchmarks from your VMs in the target region so we include your network path. our bench harness can run from your test hosts.
[06:46] Priya: what's the expected p95 at 200 concurrency for a 30-token streaming prompt on dedicated?
[06:53] Lena: if you size to reserve enough GPUs to keep batch sizes small, we typically see p95 120-180ms for that profile. if shared or autoscaled slowly, it can spike to 300-500ms until pods scale. that's why reserved pools help.
[07:10] Marcus: we heard about smart routing and fallbacks — if one region hits capacity, what's the failover behavior?
[07:17] Samir: requests can be routed by policy — latency-first, cost-first, or region. automatic fallback will hit another compatible model variant (e.g., slightly lower quality quantized model) to keep responses within SLOs. all of this is configurable per route.
[07:32] Priya: we also want transparent cost breakdown for token-level usage and per-route latency.
[07:38] Lena: Redwood Console gives token-level cost buckets, p95 per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks that pin calls to model versions.
[07:46] Derek: can we set per-route rollout policies — canary, A/B?
[07:50] Samir: yes, you can configure canary percentages, automatic rollback rules for quality regressions, and tie alerts to prompt eval sets.
[07:58] Priya: one more on benchmarks — do you support GPUs of different types? we plan to test A100 vs H100 vs Grace if needed.
[08:06] Lena: we support a range; kernel selection adapts. A100/ H100 differences show mostly on long-context and larger models; we can run the same harness on different instance types and report normalized tokens/sec and per-token cost.
[08:20] Marcus: any typical numbers you can share quickly for p95/lower config?
[08:25] Lena: anecdotal: small-medium LLMs on dedicated H100 — first token 30-70ms, p95 80-220ms depending on sequence length. But we'll produce exact numbers from your prompts.
[08:36] Priya: for our fraud model we need deterministic behavior — is there nondeterminism introduced by continuous batching?
[08:44] Lena: batching can reorder generation slightly if you use stochastic sampling; if determinism is required, we recommend setting deterministic sampling or pinned seeds and smaller batch sizes. dedicated pools also reduce variability.
[08:58] Derek: on-day-2 ops — what observability do we get?
[09:03] Samir: Console has per-token latency breakdowns, trace IDs, cold-start counters, and alerting hooks. we can stream logs to your SIEM or S3.
[09:12] Marcus: pricing — how does dedicated billing look? is it reserved monthly commitment?
[09:18] Samir: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits; we also offer burst capacity on top for spikes. hosted is usage-based per-token. we'll include pricing tiers in the follow-up.
[09:30] Priya: any concerns with data retention for logs and PII?
[09:35] Samir: we support configurable retention, redact hooks, and field-level masking. private deployments allow you to keep logs inside your VPC.
[09:44] Marcus: excellent. let's talk about the benchmark plan specifics — we need runs at 50/100/200/400 concurrency, streams on/off, 3 replications.
[09:52] Lena: noted. please share prompt corpus and we will run the harness and return p50/p95/p99 and token/sec curves plus per-token traces.
[10:01] Priya: can you also include cost estimates per 1M tokens and per-concurrency-hour on dedicated vs hosted?
[10:07] Samir: yes we'll include normalized cost charts and perf per dollar.
[10:13] Marcus: security-wise, we need to see SOC2 Type II report and an initial network diagram for private.
[10:20] Samir: we'll put both in the follow-up package.
[10:24] [Silence / notes]
[30:00] Lena: (benchmark details) when running token/sec tests we instrument kernel time, kv cache hits, and per-request queue time — sometimes transcripts show 'TV cache' in auto text but it's KV cache.
[35:00] Priya: ok thanks for that tip, we've seen weird transcription naming in other calls.
[40:00] Derek: one last question — are there SLA credits for missing p95 on dedicated?
[40:07] Samir: yes, dedicated can include SLA-backed uptime and latency credits; exact terms are contract dependent.
[45:00] Marcus: recap: Samir to send pricing & SOC2, Lena to share harness + run benchmarks after we send prompt set, Nova to provide prompt mix and target p95s and concurrency.
[45:20] Priya: i'll share prompt set by EOD Monday.
[45:25] Samir: great, we'll target running the first bench the following week.
[45:32] Lena: i'll include a short runbook for running the test from your infra so network path is included.
[45:40] Marcus: thanks everyone.
[45:45] Samir: thanks all, talk soon.
